newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling gains vs dlr on bargain hunting.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling gains vs dlr on bargain hunting.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling made further gains against the dollar on Wednesday on bargain-hunting for dollars amid higher supply from exporters.
"Sentiment is now for a stronger shilling. Now that the market has calmed down, it looks like importers think the rates (of 59 and above) are too lofty," a senior dealer said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling rate of 58.81 against the dollar compared to 59.01 on Tuesday while against the pound, the shilling was posted at 98.80 from 99.04.

Panic-triggered demand from foreign investors due to political unrest in the country on July 7 was the main reason the shilling depreciation, rapidly reaching levels as low as 61.50 against the dollar from 55 in the span of a week.
But they said foreign demand had waned adding that the market had stabilized.
At midday, dealers said they were selling dollars at 58.60 from the morning's opening of 58.90.
"A few dollars came in from tea exporters and we're expecting some more from coffee some time this week," another dealer said.
The money market was liquid. Overnight rates were quoted at between five and 15 percent compared to 5-8 percent on Tuesday.
